items.title: Oscar Rouzan Interview, 1972-12-12
items.q: But why I didn't go to Dave was all on account of the tone.

ctx.x: We didn't tell all of our names, you told yours, but Lars, you want to put your name on? Yeah, Lars, here's the dog. And my name is Dick Allen, so we know. And what's today's date? I can't remember. It's December? I'll have to look on this. Wait a minute, I've got a watch here. You know what? December 12, 1972, and the address is 1863 Industry Street, which is your home. You own it? Yeah. Did you build it yourself? Yeah. Painted it? Yeah. You know how to paint it? No, you've got a good reputation as a painter.

He played something. Yeah, he had a nice style. It's part of, you know, old time, let's see, like, which style he played? Well, he copied, you know, a little bit of Armstrong and maybe a little bit of the other type of blues type of trumpet player. I wanted to ask you more about your teachers, too, and how they would teach. Well, teaching for that, if I go to style my brother, which was the first teacher, he was tone conscious. And I spent a lot of time in sudden tone, you know, building up. And he was a type of…

Yeah, that's just... Yeah, I dropped it a few times later. I was going to go see it. Your daughter's like Texas? One, the other one don't, but one, you know, I have one like Texas. I have an idea about... Yeah, well, first thing I could ask you is what your full name is. Yeah, Oscar, Jill and Rusevans. Just a second now. I'll let you go second on that because we were four Rusevans. At the time, we were four Oscar, Jill and Rusevans. Four generations of Rusevans. In fact, I got a picture somewhere around with the…
